messages:
incident-bot: Pager — hosted-runtime/kvcache: high OOM rate on worker pool 'hosted-us-west-2-w-7' (triggered 3126337000)
incident-bot: Symptoms: repeated GPU OOMs, KV cache growth > 12GB in 30s, sustained continuous-batching backlog, 502s for generation requests. Top traces point to long prompt sessions with huge prefix amplification.

mike_oncall: taking this. thanks for the page. I see error spike in Sentry and a bunch of 137s in kube. On it.

ashley_reliability: noted — looks like prefetch + kv-cache window blowup we saw in feb. early hypothesis: runaway context amplification from a customer sending long logs + aggressive prefetch.

mike_oncall: can someone post the short query that reproduces? need to triage quickly. Also @eng-bot can we throttle new hosts into the pool?

eng-bot: autoscaler: paused scale-up to hosted-us-west-2-w-7 per request from @mike_oncall (cmd: `/autoscaler pause --pool hosted-us-west-2-w-7`)

mike_oncall: thanks. steps I'm taking: 1) disable prefetch for hosted pool 2) apply emergency kv cache caps on the runtime 3) divert traffic to fallback model variant.

ashley_reliability: +1. We should reduce continuous batch window too — it's amplifying memory use. Suggest: set `continuous_batch.max_tokens=512` and `kvcache.max_entries=2000` temporarily.

sara_prod: copying a snippet of hotfix config I'm pushing to the runtime-hosted helm release: 
```yaml
resources:
  kvcache:
    enabled: true
    max_entries: 2000 # emergency cap
    max_prefetch_tokens: 512
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  max_tokens: 512
  max_batch_size: 8
  idle_flush_ms: 15
```

mike_oncall: deploying the above as 3126337112-hotfix (canary -> pool). will watch mem + tail logs.

eng-bot: deploy bot: started rollout 3126337112 to hosted-us-west-2-w-7 (user: mike_oncall)

devops_kate: heads up — that will reduce throughput. Are we okay with extra latency?

mike_oncall: yes — prefer stable with increased latency for affected traffic. We'll route high-throughput customers to dedicated pool.

jake_csm: FYI — got ping from one customer on API errors. ETA to notify impacted customers? We likely have a handful of sessions failing.

mike_oncall: Jake — can you collate customer list from 15:40-15:55 UTC? We'll prioritize outreach. Also ask them to retry.

jake_csm: on it. sending initial note to SSO owners now.

eng-bot: deploy bot: rollout 3126337112 completed to 30% of nodes in pool (3126337164). No immediate OOMs in canary nodes.

mike_oncall: good. bump to 60% and continue observing. also applying runtime flag to disable prefetch entirely for sessions > 16k tokens: `--prefetch-window-threshold=16384`

ashley_reliability: adding a temporary KV eviction policy: LRU aggressive for entries > 4096 tokens. This should prevent slow growth.

sara_prod: pushed eviction rule via config endpoint: `POST /admin/kvcache/eviction` payload `{ "policy": "lru", "token_threshold": 4096 }`

eng-bot: metrics: mem_usage host hosted-us-west-2-w-7 dropped from 98% -> 62% over 2 min after canary changes (3126337201). CPU steady.

mike_oncall: great. I'm going to route all new long-prompt sessions to a fallback lightweight model until we stabilize. applying routing rule now.

eng-bot: routing: new sessions with prompt_length > 12000 redirected to model 'redwood-lite-1' (rule active 3126337228)

devops_kate: logging note: we'll need to keep an eye on cost with fallback routing. Also record exact git commits for the hotfix.

mike_oncall: commit hash for hotfix: `a4f3b2c9` deployed as 3126337112.

jake_csm: quick update — initial customer triage: 4 customers with errors, highest priority app had ~120 failed requests, others intermittent. I've opened a CS ticket for each.

ashley_reliability: recommend we keep caps for 4 hours, then relax gradually. Also schedule a brief postmortem to inspect continuous-batching controller metrics and prefetch heuristics.

mike_oncall: agreed. I'll keep the incident open for another 2 hours. Can someone annotate the incident channel with the mitigation steps? need concise runbook for followups.

sara_prod: summarizing mitigation steps (for postmortem):
- paused autoscaler for pool `hosted-us-west-2-w-7`
- deployed hotfix 3126337112 with KV caps and reduced continuous_batch window
- disabled aggressive prefetch for sessions > 16k tokens
- enabled aggressive LRU eviction for large entries
- routed new long-prompt sessions to fallback model `redwood-lite-1`

mike_oncall: logs show OOMs stopped after 3126337190. continuing to monitor. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

eng-bot: alert: sustained errors dropped to normal baseline at 3126337300 — incident-bot will keep record.

devops_kate: assigning followups: (1) increase prefetch safety checks in runtime (owner: ashley_reliability), (2) add KVCACHE size gating per-session (owner: sara_prod), (3) add alert that correlates kvcache growth with prompt-length (owner: mike_oncall).

ashley_reliability: will take (1). will open a RFC for safer prefetch heuristics and add unit tests.

mike_oncall: I'll create the postmortem doc and link to this thread. good job team. closing incident when metrics stable for 1 hour.

jake_csm: I'll follow up with customers once the GA incident note is ready.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (3126337345).
